claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
The high-purity baseline is fully homogeneous, has minimal impurity content, and has a uniform grain structure.
Oxygen or carbon introduced during processing segregates to grain boundaries in CoCrFeMnNi.
The introduced impurities diffuse and segregate to grain boundaries under service-like conditions.
Grain-boundary segregation of oxygen or carbon reduces local grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesive strength predisposes the alloy to intergranular cracking under mechanical stress.
Impurity-induced grain-boundary weakening causes a transition from ductile transgranular fracture to brittle intergranular fracture.
Impurity-doped samples will have lower fracture toughness than otherwise identically tested high-purity samples.
Fracture surfaces of impurity-doped samples will be dominated by brittle intergranular cracks.
High-purity samples will predominantly exhibit ductile transgranular fracture.
The proposed mechanism applies during tensile and fatigue loading from room temperature to 300 °C under controlled atmospheric oxygen levels.
The governing behavior may differ at extreme high temperatures or under highly oxidative conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says similar toughness and fracture modes despite the impurity difference are sufficient to falsify the hypothesis, whereas the formal falsification rule additionally requires comparable grain-boundary impurity segregation. These criteria can yield different conclusions if segregation increases without changing toughness or fracture mode.
